reference.title: Dumbbell Seated External Rotation (male)
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the forearm rotates up, breathe in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2.5 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3); no pain
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a slightly heavier dumbbell

cues.text: Sit on a bench with the right foot up on the bench, knee bent and raised. Rest the right elbow on the knee, upper arm out in front and a little to the side, elbow bent 90 degrees, forearm pointing forward and down, palm down.
Breathe out and turn the forearm up about the elbow until it points up; the elbow stays on the knee.
Forearm vertical, palm forward; shoulder down and back.
Breathe in and lower slowly to the start.
Pause and repeat. Then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow sliding off or lifting from the knee
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow resting on the knee as the pivot.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to lift the weight
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and still; only the forearm moves.
Keep the shoulder down and away from the ear.

kinematics.norm: From the forearm forward and below horizontal up to vertical (clinical opinion); external rotation with the arm abducted and supported loads the infraspinatus and teres minor (Reinold 2004)
Upper arm forward and out (scapular plane), elbow supported on the raised knee (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #15725, Dumbbell Seated External Rotation (male), video (movement reference only; page not read)

Reinold, Wilk, Fleisig, Zheng, Barrentine, Chmielewski, Cody, Jameson and Andrews 2004, electromyographic analysis of the rotator cuff and deltoid musculature during common shoulder external rotation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 34(7):385-394)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Rotator cuff work: use a light dumbbell and a slow, pain-free range.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: rest the elbow lower (less elevation) and shorten the range.
Hip or knee discomfort with the foot up: rest the elbow on a padded box instead.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): turns the forearm up (external rotation).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Assists external rotation with the arm forward and out.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Light: steadies the arm on the knee.

guides.label: Forearm turns up about the elbow
